agree.reason: The tone is warm and honest, but a backer who has lost money on a first-time creator gets no delivery date, no refund promise and no update schedule, so the wariest reader is unlikely to pledge.

honest.reason: The draft rightly drops the 'proven hit' claim, but it calls the 23 ratings 'an honest one' without saying most came from people who played at the creator's own convention table, and 'most of the rest pays for shipping' is not checked against fees.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are repeated rather than worked out: there is no breakdown of $28,000 minus $17,400 for the factory and about $2,800 in fees, no backer count needed to reach the goal (about 572), and no comparison of that count with the 1,240 people on the email list.

right_comparison.reason: It never puts this campaign beside the alternative the reader fears, a typical first-time project with unfinished art and no factory quote, even though the finished art, finished rules and signed quote make that contrast possible.

qualification.reason: The risks section hedges with 'won't promise dates I can't keep' and 'if anything slips' but names no November delivery date, no updates every two weeks and no refund if delivery is more than three months late, so the reader has nothing to check.

objections.reason: It names the first-time-creator worry but answers it only loosely; it leaves out the signed quote, the finished art, the reviewer's video in launch week and the refund commitment, which are the facts that would actually meet that objection.

fit.reason: It is a crowdfunding pitch of about 500 words, but it uses '[Game Title]' and '[Add backer-only extras]' placeholders where the real name was available and stretch goals can't be promised, and it leaves out the creator's name and the campaign dates.
